label: 現代小説
description: 2000年以降の世界の文学シーンを牽引する作家たち。ブッカー賞、全米図書賞、ピューリッツァー賞受賞作を中心に。

books.title: Flights
books.author: Olga Tokarczuk
books.authorJa: オルガ・トカルチュク
books.descriptionJa: 2018年ノーベル文学賞受賞作家による、移動と断片の文学。空港、ホテル、匿名の都市を舞台に、解剖学から旅行記、神話から現代の難民問題まで、旅する身体をめぐる無数の物語が星座のように結びつく。章ごとに読む順番を変えても成立する、自由な構造。
books.whyReadJa: 現代ヨーロッパ文学の最高峰の一つ。従来の「小説」の枠を超えた断片形式が、SNS時代の感覚に驚くほどマッチする。ポーランド文学の豊かさを知る入口にも。
books.selectionReasonJa: ノーベル賞作家トカルチュクの、断片と移動の文学。
books.descriptionEn: A work of travel and fragments from the winner of the 2018 Nobel Prize in Literature. Set against airports, hotels, anonymous cities, and border crossings, countless stories of the traveling body—ranging from anatomy and dissection to travelogues, from ancient myth to the modern refugee crisis—constellate and connect like a constellation in the night sky. Its free-form structure holds together even when the chapters are read in a different order, and the reader is invited to enter and leave at any point, making it a genuinely open work.
books.whyReadEn: One of the pinnacles of contemporary European literature. Its fragmentary form, which breaks through the conventional frame of the novel, matches the sensibility of the social-media age astonishingly well. It is also a rewarding gateway to the richness of Polish literature, which remains little known outside its borders.

books.title: My Brilliant Friend
books.author: Elena Ferrante
books.authorJa: エレナ・フェッランテ
books.descriptionJa: 1950年代ナポリの貧困地区で育った二人の少女、レヌーとリラの60年にわたる友情と競争。学ぶことで階級を抜け出そうとするレヌーと、天才的な知性を持ちながら取り残されるリラ。女性の生きづらさ、暴力、そして知への渇望を描いて世界を熱狂させた「ナポリの物語」四部作の第一作。
books.whyReadJa: 世界で最も読まれている現代文学シリーズ。読者を「次が気になる」で止められなくさせる物語の力がここにある。フェミニズム文学の枠を超えた普遍性。
books.selectionReasonJa: 世界で最も読まれる現代文学シリーズ。フェッランテの「ナポリの物語」開幕。
books.descriptionEn: Two girls, Elena and Lila, grow up in the poverty-stricken district of 1950s Naples, bound together by sixty years of friendship, rivalry, and envy. Lenu tries to escape her class through education, while Lila, gifted with a dazzling and restless intelligence, is left behind in the neighborhood. A portrait of women's hardship, domestic violence, and hunger for knowledge that electrified readers around the world—the first novel in the Neapolitan Quartet, which became a global phenomenon.
books.whyReadEn: The most widely read contemporary literary series in the world. Here is storytelling power that makes readers unable to stop, always hungry for what happens next. Its universality reaches far beyond the category of feminist literature, speaking to anyone who has ever had a friend who is also a rival.

books.title: Normal People
books.author: Sally Rooney
books.descriptionJa: アイルランドの小さな町からダブリンの大学まで——コネルとマリアンヌ、階級の異なる二人の若者がすれ違いながら惹かれ合う。「声に出して言えないこと」がすべてを動かす、切なくて鋭い恋愛小説。ミレニアル世代のディケンズと呼ばれるルーニーの世界的ベストセラー。
books.whyReadJa: 現代の恋愛とコミュニケーション不全をこれほど精緻に書ける作家はいない。フェッランテ『リナと私』好きにも響く。英語が平易で洋書入門にも。
books.selectionReasonJa: 現代の恋愛とコミュニケーション不全を精緻に描く、ルーニーの世界的ベストセラー。
books.descriptionEn: From a small Irish town to the university in Dublin—Connell and Marianne, two young people from different classes, keep drifting apart and keep being drawn back to one another through years of misunderstanding and longing. A tender, razor-sharp love story in which everything is set in motion by what cannot be said aloud, by the things both of them fail to voice. A global bestseller by Rooney, who has been called the Dickens of the millennial generation.
books.whyReadEn: No writer today renders modern love and the failure of communication so precisely, with such emotional and psychological accuracy. It will resonate deeply with fans of Ferrante's My Brilliant Friend. The English is plain and accessible, making it a fine gateway into reading books in the original language.

books.title: Girl, Woman, Other
books.titleJa: ガール、ウーマン、アザー
books.author: Bernardine Evaristo
books.authorJa: バーナーディン・エヴァリスト
books.descriptionJa: イギリスに生きる12人の黒人女性たち——10代から90代まで、移民、レズビアン、ノンバイナリー、シングルマザー——その人生が交錯する多声的小説。ブッカー賞をマーガレット・アトウッドと同時受賞した問題作。詩のような散文で書かれ、声を奪われてきた人たちに声を与える。
books.whyReadJa: 現代イギリス文学の到達点であり、フェミニズムと人種の交差点を見事に描く。多声的な語りが好きな人（パムク『わたしの名は赤』好き）に。
books.selectionReasonJa: 12人の黒人女性を描く、ブッカー賞受賞の多声的小説。
books.descriptionEn: Twelve Black women living in Britain—from their teens to their nineties, immigrants, lesbians, nonbinary people, single mothers, artists, and academics—whose lives brush against and intersect one another in this polyphonic, radically inventive novel. Written in prose that reads like poetry, without conventional punctuation, it gives voice to people who have long been silenced. A controversial landmark that shared the Booker Prize with Margaret Atwood.
books.whyReadEn: A high-water mark of contemporary British literature that brilliantly maps the crossroads of feminism and race, of class and identity. Perfect for lovers of polyphonic narration—including fans of Pamuk's My Name Is Red—who want to see how a chorus of voices can be assembled into a single powerful story.

books.title: On Earth We're Briefly Gorgeous
books.titleJa: この地上で、ぼくらはつかのま輝く
books.author: Ocean Vuong
books.descriptionJa: ベトナム系移民の母に、文字の読めない母のために英語で綴られた手紙——詩人として名高いヴオンの初小説は、戦争のトラウマ、母と子の暴力と愛、クィアの目覚めを、一行一行が詩のように美しい散文で描く。移民文学とクィア文学の新しい到達点。
books.whyReadJa: 言葉がこれほど美しくなれるのかと呆然とする。『シンパサイザー』（ウェン）と合わせて読むと、ベトナム戦争後の世代が文学で何を成し遂げたかが見える。
books.selectionReasonJa: 移民とクィアの物語を詩のような散文で描く、ヴオンの初小説。
books.descriptionEn: A letter written in English to a Vietnamese immigrant mother who cannot read it, framed as a novel. Vuong's debut—by the celebrated poet—tells of the trauma of war passed down through generations, the violence and tenderness between mother and son, and the awakening of a queer identity, all rendered in prose where every line is as beautiful as poetry. A new high-water mark for both immigrant literature and queer literature.
books.whyReadEn: You will be stunned to discover that words can be this beautiful, this precise. Read alongside Nguyen's The Sympathizer, and you will see what the generation after the Vietnam War has achieved in literature, transforming inherited wounds into art that speaks across the world.

books.title: Homegoing
books.author: Yaa Gyasi
books.descriptionJa: 18世紀ガーナ——奴隷貿易でアメリカに売られた姉と、奴隷商人と結婚した妹。その子孫たちの300年にわたる物語を、一世代一章で紡ぐ壮大なデビュー作。アフリカとアメリカ、自由と束縛、記憶と忘却が交錯する。全米図書賞候補、26歳の新星が書いたアフリカン・ディアスポラの叙事詩。
books.whyReadJa: 『崩れゆく絆』（アチェベ）と『世界と僕のあいだで』（コーツ）を繋ぐ、アフリカからアメリカへの300年の架け橋。歴史が個人にどう刻まれるかを物語る力作。
books.selectionReasonJa: 300年の奴隷制の遺産を一族の物語で描く、ジャシのデビュー作。
books.descriptionEn: Eighteenth-century Ghana: an elder sister is sold into the American slave trade, while her younger sister marries a white slaver. From this fork in the road, the novel traces their descendants across three hundred years, one generation per chapter, from the dungeons of Cape Coast to the coal mines of the American South and beyond. A National Book Award finalist, this epic of the African diaspora was written by a rising star of twenty-six.
books.whyReadEn: A three-hundred-year bridge from Africa to America, connecting Achebe's Things Fall Apart to Coates's Between the World and Me. A powerful work that shows precisely how history is inscribed on individual lives, one generation after another, and how the past never really lets anyone go.

books.title: The Underground Railroad
books.author: Colson Whitehead
books.authorJa: コルソン・ホワイトヘッド
books.descriptionJa: 19世紀アメリカ南部——奴隷制から逃れるための秘密結社「地下鉄道」が、ここでは実際に地下を走る列車として描かれる。逃亡奴隷コーラの逃避行をSF的に変奏しながら、アメリカの人種差別の根源を暴く。ピューリッツァー賞と全米図書賞をW受賞した現代文学のマイルストーン。
books.whyReadJa: アメリカの人種差別の歴史を、息をのむストーリーテリングで読める。『世界と僕のあいだで』の理論編に対し、こちらは小説編。重いテーマをエンタメに昇華する技がすごい。
books.selectionReasonJa: ピューリッツァー賞・全米図書賞W受賞。奴隷制を歴史修正ファンタジーで描く。
books.descriptionEn: Nineteenth-century American South: here the Underground Railroad, the secret network that helped slaves escape to freedom, is imagined as an actual train running through tunnels beneath the earth. Following the fugitive slave Cora's flight from Georgia, Whitehead transposes history into a speculative, almost fantastical key while exposing the deep roots of American racism in all their horror. A milestone of contemporary literature, winner of both the Pulitzer Prize and the National Book Award.
books.whyReadEn: The history of American racism told through breathtaking, page-turning storytelling. If Coates's Between the World and Me is the theoretical counterpart, this is the novelistic one. The craft of elevating a heavy, painful theme into riveting entertainment is quite simply remarkable.

books.title: A Little Life
books.author: Hanya Yanagihara
books.descriptionJa: NYで出会った4人の青年の人生を、特にトラウマを抱えたジュードを中心に描く800ページの大河小説。友情とは、愛とは、生き延びることとは何かを問い、世界中の読者の心を抉った。ブッカー賞最終候補。賛否両論を巻き起こすほどの衝撃力を秘めた、現代版『嵐が丘』。
books.whyReadJa: 感情を揺さぶる小説の力を信じている人に。長いが、読後には「読んでよかった」と必ず思う。人生で最も泣いた本になるかもしれない。
books.selectionReasonJa: 友情とトラウマを800ページで描く、感情を揺さぶる現代の大河。
books.descriptionEn: An 800-page saga of four young men who meet in New York after college, centered on Jude, who carries a traumatic past that is revealed only gradually. Through decades of friendship, success, and suffering, it asks what friendship is, what love is, and what it means to survive. A Booker Prize finalist, it has been called a modern Wuthering Heights for its explosive emotional power, and it has divided readers like few other books of its time.
books.whyReadEn: For readers who believe in the power of fiction to move them to the core. Long, but by the end you will surely feel it was worth every page. It may well become the book that makes you cry the most in your life—a reading experience you will not forget.

books.title: Lincoln in the Bardo
books.titleJa: リンカーンとさまよえる霊魂たち
books.author: George Saunders
books.authorJa: ジョージ・ソーンダーズ
books.descriptionJa: リンカーン大統領の11歳の息子が病死し、父親は墓に何度も足を運んで遺体を抱きしめた——この史実を元に、墓地に閉じ込められた霊魂たちの声だけで構成された異形の小説。ブッカー賞受賞。生者と死者の対話から浮かび上がる、喪失と愛の物語。前代未聞の語りが生み出す感動。
books.whyReadJa: 現代アメリカ文学の最高の実験。語りがこんなに自由でいいのかと驚く。ジョーン・ディディオン『悲しみにある者は』と対になる、もう一つの「喪の文学」。
books.selectionReasonJa: 霊魂たちの声だけで構成された、ブッカー賞受賞の実験文学。
books.descriptionEn: When Abraham Lincoln's eleven-year-old son Willie dies in 1862, the president repeatedly visits the crypt to embrace the body. From this historical fact, Saunders constructs an unorthodox novel narrated entirely by the ghosts trapped in the Georgetown cemetery, whose chattering, overlapping voices form a strange chorus. A Booker Prize winner. From the dialogue between the living and the dead emerges a moving story of loss, grief, and love, created through a narrative mode never seen before.
books.whyReadEn: The finest experiment in contemporary American literature. You will marvel that narration can be this free, this inventive, and this moving. Read together with Joan Didion's The Year of Magical Thinking, it forms a second literature of mourning—one that finds grace inside the chaos of grief.

books.title: Outline
books.author: Rachel Cusk
books.descriptionJa: 離婚したばかりの女性作家がアテネで創作講座を教える——ただそれだけの小説。しかし彼女が出会う人々が語り出す人生の断片が、小説という形式そのものを問い直す。「ほとんど何も起きない」のに「すべてが起きている」と評される新しい文学の形。
books.whyReadJa: プロットに頼らず「人の話を聞くこと」だけで成立する小説の革新。静かでいて中毒性がある。エルノーやトカルチュクの断片文学が好きなら。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「人の話を聞くこと」だけで成立する、小説形式を問い直した傑作。
books.descriptionEn: A recently divorced woman writer goes to Athens to teach a creative writing course—that is, essentially, all that happens. But the strangers she meets, each of whom tells her the story of his or her life in long monologues, transform the book into an inquiry into the very form of the novel. Praised as a book in which almost nothing happens while everything happens, it proposes a radically new kind of literary shape, held together by listening alone.
books.whyReadEn: An innovation: a novel built not on plot but purely on the act of listening to other people's stories. Quiet, restrained, and yet strangely addictive. If you love the fragmentary literature of Annie Ernaux and Olga Tokarczuk, this is essential reading.

books.title: White Teeth
books.author: Zadie Smith
books.descriptionJa: ロンドン——バングラデシュ系、ジャマイカ系、ユダヤ系、イギリス人の家族が織りなす多文化コメディ。24歳で書かれたデビュー作が世界中でベストセラーになり、「多文化主義文学」の旗手を生んだ。移民の世代間ギャップ、宗教、遺伝子操作までを痛快に描く。
books.whyReadJa: 現代ロンドンの縮図のような小説。多様性について笑いながら考えたい人に。エヴァリスト『ガール、ウーマン、アザー』とあわせて読むとイギリス多文化文学の地図ができる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 多文化主義文学の旗手スミスの、痛快なデビュー作。
books.descriptionEn: London—a rollicking multicultural comedy woven from the lives of Bangladeshi, Jamaican, Jewish, and English families whose paths cross over three generations. Written when its author was just twenty-four, this debut became a worldwide bestseller and made Zadie Smith the standard-bearer of multicultural literature. With enormous verve and wit, it takes on generational gaps among immigrants, religion, and even genetic engineering, without ever losing its warmth.
books.whyReadEn: A novel that reads like a miniature portrait of modern London in all its chaotic diversity. For anyone who wants to think seriously about diversity while laughing out loud. Paired with Evaristo's Girl, Woman, Other, it completes a vivid map of British multicultural literature.

books.title: The Nickel Boys
books.author: Colson Whitehead
books.authorJa: コルソン・ホワイトヘッド
books.descriptionJa: 1960年代フロリダの少年院で実際に起きた虐待と殺人を基にした、静かで激しい告発の文学。黒人少年エルウッドは無実の罪で収容され、「ニッケル・アカデミー」の地獄を生き延びる。ピューリッツァー賞を2度受賞したホワイトヘッドのもう一つの傑作。短くて痛烈。
books.whyReadJa: 『地下鉄道』よりも短く、より現実に近い分だけ心に刺さる。人種不正義についての最も重要な近年の小説の一つ。学びながら深く揺さぶられる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 少年院の虐待を告発する、ピューリッツァー賞受賞作。
books.descriptionEn: A quiet, fierce work of accusation based on the real abuse and murder that took place at a Florida reform school in the 1960s. Elwood, a Black teenager with a bright future, is sent away for a crime he did not commit and must survive the hell of the Nickel Academy, where boys are beaten, starved, and worse. A finalist for the Pulitzer, which Whitehead went on to win, this is his other masterpiece—short, restrained, and searingly painful.
books.whyReadEn: Shorter than The Underground Railroad and closer to historical reality, it cuts even deeper. One of the most important recent novels about racial injustice in America. You will be shaken to the core, and the education it offers is inseparable from the emotion it stirs.

books.title: The Sympathizer
books.author: Viet Thanh Nguyen
books.authorJa: ヴィエト・タン・ウェン
books.descriptionJa: ベトナム戦争後、南ベトナムの将軍の副官としてアメリカに亡命した共産党の二重スパイ。二つの世界に引き裂かれた男の告白という形式で、難民、アイデンティティ、戦争の記憶を描く。ピューリッツァー賞受賞。ハリウッドで映像化もされた現代アメリカ文学のマイルストーン。
books.whyReadJa: ベトナム戦争を「アメリカの悲劇」ではなくベトナム人の目線で語り直す、目から鱗の一冊。難民としての視点は、日本で暮らす私たちにも響く。
books.selectionReasonJa: ベトナム戦争を二重スパイの視点で描く、ピューリッツァー賞受賞作。
books.descriptionEn: After the fall of Saigon, a Communist double agent flees to America disguised as the aide to a South Vietnamese general. In the form of a confession by a man torn between two countries, two ideologies, and two selves, the novel explores the refugee experience, fractured identity, and the memory of war with dark humor and relentless intelligence. A Pulitzer Prize winner and later adapted for television, it is a milestone of contemporary American literature.
books.whyReadEn: An eye-opening book that retells the Vietnam War from Vietnamese eyes rather than as an American tragedy, overturning decades of received narrative. Its refugee perspective, its sense of living between worlds, resonates strongly with those of us living in Japan today.

books.title: Never Let Me Go
books.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
books.descriptionJa: 寄宿学校ヘイルシャムで育てられたキャシーたちは、特別な使命のために生まれた存在だった。日常の淡い光の下で、その事実が少しずつ明らかになっていく。ノーベル文学賞作家イシグロが、愛と喪失をSFの装置で描いた、静かで痛ましい傑作。
books.whyReadJa: 『クララとお日さま』と対になる、イシグロのSF的傑作。クローン技術が当たり前になった世界で「人間とは何か」を問う。
books.selectionReasonJa: ノーベル賞作家イシグロが愛と喪失をSFで描いた傑作。
books.descriptionEn: Kathy and her friends, raised at the secluded boarding school of Hailsham, have always known that they are special—but only gradually do they come to understand what their specialness means. They were created, and are being raised, for a single purpose: to donate their organs until they complete. Under the pale, gentle light of everyday life, this truth slowly surfaces. Nobel laureate Ishiguro's quiet, heartbreaking masterpiece uses the machinery of science fiction to tell a story of love, loss, and human dignity.
books.whyReadEn: Ishiguro's science-fictional masterpiece, best read as a companion to Klara and the Sun. In a world where cloning is simply taken for granted, it asks what it means to be human, what we owe one another, and what we allow ourselves not to see.

books.title: The Remains of the Day
books.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
books.descriptionJa: 老執事スティーブンスは、戦後イギリスの田舎を一人旅しながら、かつて仕えた侯爵家での日々を回想する。「尊厳」を追求するあまり、恋と歴史の転換点を逃してしまった男の物語。ブッカー賞受賞。映画化もされたイシグロの代表作。
books.whyReadJa: 語らないことの雄弁さ。言葉の裏側を読む文学の快楽がここにある。ゼーバルト的な「記憶の修復」をより抑制的に描く。
books.selectionReasonJa: 語らないことの雄弁さ。ブッカー賞受賞のイシグロ代表作。
books.descriptionEn: In post-war England, Stevens, an elderly butler of the old school, drives across the countryside on a motoring holiday, recalling his decades of service to the great house of Darlington Hall. In his formal, carefully controlled narration, we glimpse what he will never admit: that in his rigid pursuit of professional dignity he missed both the love of his life and the moral turning points of history. A Booker Prize winner, later adapted into an acclaimed film, and Ishiguro's most representative work.
books.whyReadEn: The eloquence of what is left unsaid. Here is the pleasure of literature read between the lines, where every evasion speaks louder than any declaration. A memory-restoration in the manner of Sebald, but rendered with even greater restraint and control.

books.title: The Buried Giant
books.author: Kazuo Ishiguro
books.descriptionJa: アーサー王の死後、霧の国ブリテン。老いた夫婦は、記憶を消す「忘却の霧」が立ちこめる土地を旅して、遠い昔に別れた息子を探す。記憶の呪いと和解をめぐる、中世イングランドを舞台にした寓話。トールキン以後のイギリス幻想文学に位置づけられる異色作。
books.whyReadJa: 「忘れること」と「思い出すこと」のどちらが赦しなのか——人間の記憶の本質を問う、イシグロらしい寓話。
books.selectionReasonJa: 記憶の本質を問う、中世英国を舞台にしたイシグロの寓話。
books.descriptionEn: Britain in the misty years after the death of King Arthur. An elderly couple, Axl and Beatrice, set out across a land covered by a strange fog of forgetfulness—a mist that erases memory, and with it the crimes of the past—in search of the son they parted from long ago. Along the way they meet knights, monsters, and a Saxon warrior. A fable set in medieval England about the curse of memory and the price of reconciliation, and an unusual work within the British fantasy tradition that followed Tolkien.
books.whyReadEn: Which is forgiveness: forgetting, or remembering? A fable very much in Ishiguro's mode, probing the very nature of human memory and asking whether a nation can heal itself by burying its past. Quiet, strange, and deeply moving.

books.title: The Memory Police
books.author: Yoko Ogawa
books.descriptionJa: 島の上の秘密の国で、「もの」が次々と記憶ごと消去されていく。消されたものの記憶を失わないために、作家の彼女はそれを心に留め続ける。カズオ・イシグロや村上春樹とも共振する、喪失と抵抗をめぐる静かな寓話。国際ブッカー賞候補作。
books.whyReadJa: 「消える記憶」をテーマにした日本文学が世界で高く評価された例。日本文学の新しい読み方の入口としても。
books.selectionReasonJa: 記憶を消される世界の寓話。国際ブッカー賞候補の日本文学。
books.descriptionEn: On a secret island nation, things begin to vanish—ribbons, photographs, birds—erased one by one along with all memory of them, at the command of a mysterious Memory Police. So that she will not lose what has been taken away, a writer keeps a mental record of the vanished objects and the feelings attached to them, at the risk of her own safety. A quiet, unsettling fable of loss and resistance that resonates with both Kazuo Ishiguro and Haruki Murakami. A finalist for the International Booker Prize.
books.whyReadEn: A striking example of Japanese literature on the theme of vanishing memory earning high international acclaim, and a reminder of why Ogawa's quiet stories translate so well. It also works as a doorway to a new way of reading Japanese literature.

books.title: The Sea
books.author: John Banville
books.descriptionJa: 妻を亡くした老美術史家マックス・モーデンは、少年時代を過ごした海辺の町に戻り、あの夏の記憶——親しくした家族の悲劇——を想起する。ブッカー賞受賞。散文の美しさと記憶の構造が織りなす、アイルランド文学の精緻な結晶。
books.whyReadJa: 散文そのものが芸術。記憶と喪失をめぐる最も美しい小説の一つ。ルーニーが好きならこちらも。
books.selectionReasonJa: 記憶と喪失をめぐる、ブッカー賞受賞のアイルランド文学の結晶。
books.descriptionEn: Max Morden, an elderly art historian mourning his wife, returns to the seaside village where he spent his childhood summers, and there summons the memories of that long-ago season—above all the tragedy of the well-to-do family he grew close to, and the beautiful mother who transfixed him as a boy. A Booker Prize winner. Banville's prose is widely regarded as among the most beautiful in the English language, and this novel is a refined crystallization of Irish literature, weaving the sensuous beauty of language with the intricate architecture of memory.
books.whyReadEn: The prose itself is art—every sentence is carefully shaped and resonant. One of the most beautiful novels ever written about memory and loss, about how the past keeps flowing into the present. If you love the emotional precision of Sally Rooney, this is for you too.

books.title: Atonement
books.author: Ian McEwan
books.authorJa: イアン・マキューアン
books.descriptionJa: 1935年、暑い夏の日。13歳の少女ブライオニーは、姉の恋人ロビーを犯人と誤認して告発してしまう。その一つの嘘が、愛と運命を永遠にねじ曲げる——語り、時間、罪と贖罪をめぐる現代イギリス文学の金字塔。映画化もされた名作。
books.whyReadJa: 「一つの嘘が人生を変える」物語の完成形。語りの技巧と感情の強度が合わさった、最も完成度の高い現代小説の一つ。
books.selectionReasonJa: 一つの嘘が人生を変える物語の完成形。マキューアンの代表作。
books.descriptionEn: On a hot summer's day in 1935, thirteen-year-old Briony Tallis, a precocious writer, misidentifies the man she sees at the fountain and accuses Robbie Turner—her sister's lover and the housekeeper's son—of a crime he did not commit. That single lie, born of imagination and childish certainty, twists love and destiny forever, across wartime Britain and beyond. A towering work of contemporary British literature about narrative, time, guilt, and the possibility of atonement. Acclaimed novel, later made into a celebrated film.
books.whyReadEn: The definitive telling of the story in which one lie changes a life forever. Narrative technique and emotional intensity combined at the highest level make it one of the most accomplished modern novels, a book whose final revelation forces you to rethink everything you have read.

books.title: The Line of Beauty
books.author: Alan Hollinghurst
books.authorJa: アラン・ホリングハースト
books.descriptionJa: 1980年代、サッチャー時代のイギリス。富裕層の家庭に居候する青年ニックは、美と上流社会に魅了されていく。しかし彼の欲望と無垢は、エイズと政治の荒波に呑み込まれる。ブッカー賞受賞。英国病を内側から描く、鋭く美しい小説。
books.whyReadJa: 「美」への没入がどれほど危険か。エイズ時代の同性愛をめぐる文学の最高傑作の一つ。
books.selectionReasonJa: エイズ時代のイギリスを内側から描く、ブッカー賞受賞作。
books.descriptionEn: Britain in the 1980s, the years of Margaret Thatcher. Nick Guest, a young Oxford graduate, lodges with the wealthy Fedden family and is gradually bewitched by their beauty, their elegance, and the glittering high society they inhabit. But his desire and his innocence are steadily swallowed by the twin storms of the AIDS crisis and Tory politics, until the world he so admires turns on him. A Booker Prize winner—a sharp, tender, exquisitely written novel that dissects the British condition from within.
books.whyReadEn: A reminder of how dangerous immersion in beauty can be, how seductive and how destructive. One of the finest works of literature about gay life in the AIDS era, it is also a brilliant political novel and an elegy for an entire generation.

books.title: Wolf Hall
books.author: Hilary Mantel
books.descriptionJa: 16世紀イングランド。新参者トマス・クロムウェルは、庶民の出身からヘンリー八世の腹心へと這い上がる。宗教改革、王妃の処刑、宮廷の陰謀——歴史小説の常識を覆す語りの力でブッカー賞を受賞した、現代歴史小説の金字塔。
books.whyReadJa: 歴史小説の最前線。史料の隙間から人間の息遣いを立ち上げる技は、エンタメと文学の両方で最高水準。
books.selectionReasonJa: ヘンリー八世の宮廷を描く、現代歴史小説の金字塔。
books.descriptionEn: Sixteenth-century England. Thomas Cromwell, the son of a Putney blacksmith, rises from nothing to become the most powerful man in the realm as the indispensable servant of Henry VIII. Through his eyes we witness the Reformation, the fall of Cardinal Wolsey, the execution of Anne Boleyn, and the murderous games of court intrigue. A narrative power that overturned every convention of historical fiction earned this book the Booker Prize. A pinnacle of the modern historical novel and the first of a celebrated trilogy.
books.whyReadEn: The cutting edge of historical fiction. The skill of summoning human breath, ambition, and fear from the gaps between historical documents is at the highest level in both entertainment and literature. History has rarely felt so immediate, or so dangerously alive.

books.title: The Bee Sting
books.author: Paul Murray
books.descriptionJa: アイルランドの田舎町、車修理業を営むバーンズ家。父ディックの事業は瀕死で、母イモジーンは過去の傷を抱え、息子たちはそれぞれの迷路に入り込む。四つの視点から描かれる、家族の崩壊と再生の物語。ブッカー賞候補、2020年代アイルランド文学の代表作。
books.whyReadJa: 家族小説の現代的な完成形。四人の語りが交差する構造と、ブラックユーモアの切れ味が最高。
books.selectionReasonJa: 四人の語りが交差する、2020年代アイルランド文学の代表作。
books.descriptionEn: In an Irish country town, the Barnes family runs a car repair business that is quietly falling apart. Father Dick's company is on the brink of ruin and he is being slowly conned by a smooth-talking buyer; mother Imogen carries old wounds she has never confessed; and their two children wander into mazes of their own. A story of family collapse and the possibility of renewal, told from four points of view across several decades. A Booker Prize finalist and a representative masterpiece of 2020s Irish literature.
books.whyReadEn: The modern consummation of the family novel. The structure of four intersecting voices, each withholding something from the reader, is masterful, and the edge of its black humor is supremely sharp. A long book that earns every one of its pages.

books.title: Shuggie Bain
books.author: Douglas Stuart
books.authorJa: ダグラス・スチュアート
books.descriptionJa: 1980年代グラスゴー。サッチャー時代の炭鉱町で、母アグネスのアルコール依存に翻弄されながらも、それでも母を救おうとし続ける少年シュギー。ブッカー賞受賞。自伝的要素を持つ、痛烈で美しい労働者階級の家族の物語。
books.whyReadJa: 「どうしようもない愛」をこれほど正直に書ける物語は稀。読後、しばらく余韻が抜けない一冊。
books.selectionReasonJa: ブッカー賞受賞。アルコール依存の母と少年を描く労働者階級の物語。
books.descriptionEn: Glasgow in the 1980s, under the shadow of Thatcher. In a post-industrial mining town, young Shuggie Bain is caught in the orbit of his glamorous, self-destructive mother Agnes, whose alcoholism slowly destroys everything around her. Shuggie both longs to rescue her and knows he cannot, and he is tormented by being different from the other boys. A Booker Prize winner carried by autobiographical elements, it is a fiercely beautiful, painful story of a working-class family and a child's unwavering, hopeless love.
books.whyReadEn: Rare is the story that writes hopeless, impossible love this honestly and this beautifully. The portrait of Agnes is one of the great characters of recent fiction. A book whose afterglow—and whose pain—stays with you long after you close it.

books.title: Small Things Like These
books.author: Claire Keegan
books.descriptionJa: 1985年のアイルランド。石炭商人ビル・ファーロングは、修道院で秘密に扱われる少女たちの存在を知ってしまう。黙るか、それとも声を上げるか——クリスマスを舞台にした静かな一冊が、普遍的な良心の物語として世界中で読まれた。
books.whyReadJa: たった100ページほどの短さで、これほど深い余韻を残す小説は稀。ブッカー賞候補。一気に読める。
books.selectionReasonJa: 100ページで良心を問う、ブッカー賞候補の静かな傑作。
books.descriptionEn: Ireland, 1985, at Christmastime. Bill Furlong, a coal merchant and devoted family man, is delivering fuel when he discovers that the local convent is secretly keeping girls in shameful conditions—unmarried mothers and their children, hidden away from the world. He is a man who has known poverty himself and has chosen to look away, like everyone else. To stay silent, or to raise his voice? A quiet, precisely written book that was read around the world as a universal story of conscience.
books.whyReadEn: Rare is the novel that leaves such a deep afterglow in only about a hundred pages. Short enough to read in a single sitting, it gathers enormous moral weight. A Booker Prize finalist, it is a small book with a very large conscience.

books.title: The Testaments
books.author: Margaret Atwood
books.authorJa: マーガレット・アトウッド
books.descriptionJa: 『侍女の物語』の15年後。ギレアド共和国を内側から描く三人の女性の証言を通して、全体主義国家の崩壊へ向かう力学を描く。ブッカー賞を受賞した、アトウッドのSFディストピア文学の到達点。
books.whyReadJa: 『侍女の物語』の続編にして完結編。ディストピア文学の金字塔を最後まで読みたい人に。
books.selectionReasonJa: 『侍女の物語』の続編・完結編。ブッカー賞受賞。
books.descriptionEn: Fifteen years after the events of The Handmaid's Tale, the Republic of Gilead is still standing—but cracking. Through the written testimonies of three women, including Aunt Lydia and two young women raised inside the regime, the novel reveals Gilead from within and charts the forces pulling the totalitarian state toward collapse. A Booker Prize winner, jointly with Evaristo, and the summit of Atwood's dystopian fiction, equal to and in some ways surpassing its predecessor.
books.whyReadEn: The sequel and conclusion to The Handmaid's Tale, written decades later with the perspective of our own age. For anyone who wants to see the cornerstone of dystopian literature carried through to its end, this is essential reading—a thriller, a confession, and a reckoning in one.

books.title: The Handmaid's Tale
books.author: Margaret Atwood
books.authorJa: マーガレット・アトウッド
books.descriptionJa: 環境汚染で出生率が激減した未来のアメリカ。極端な宗教国家ギレアドでは、出産可能な女性が国家の「侍女」として分配されていた。全体主義と女性の身体をめぐる、ディストピア文学の金字塔。ドラマ化で再注目された。
books.whyReadJa: 「女性の身体をめぐる政治」を描いた最も影響力のある小説。いま読むと、むしろ現代の問いが鮮明になる。
books.selectionReasonJa: ディストピア文学の金字塔。女性の身体をめぐる政治を描く。
books.descriptionEn: In a future America where environmental catastrophe has devastated fertility, an ultra-religious faction has seized power and established the Republic of Gilead. Childbearing women are stripped of their names, their freedom, and their bodies, and are distributed among the ruling class as Handmaids, their only purpose to bear children for the powerful. A cornerstone of dystopian literature about totalitarianism and the female body, told in the quiet, haunting voice of Offred. Revived to enormous new attention by its television adaptation.
books.whyReadEn: The most influential novel ever written about the politics of the female body, and it grows more urgent with each year. Reading it today, its questions—about power, control, and what can be taken from a person—feel startlingly, frighteningly current.

books.title: Open City
books.author: Teju Cole
books.descriptionJa: マンハッタンに暮らすナイジェリア系精神科医ジュリアス。彼は仕事の合間に、ニューヨークの街を延々と歩き続ける。その散歩の中で見る人々、記憶、歴史の断片が、都市と自己を織り上げる。セバルド的「歩行の文学」の現代版。
books.whyReadJa: 街を歩くことで見えてくる世界。ゼーバルトの影響を受けた、叙情と知性を併せ持つ新しい都市小説。
books.selectionReasonJa: 街を歩くことで見える世界。セバルド的「歩行の文学」の現代版。
books.descriptionEn: Julius, a Nigerian-born psychiatrist living in Manhattan, walks the streets of New York endlessly in his free hours. Over the course of the novel, his walking becomes a form of thinking: the people he meets, the memories they stir, the historical layers of the city he uncovers along the way. The city becomes a map of the self, and the self a map of history. A modern counterpart to Sebaldian literature of walking, and a quiet meditation on identity, migration, and the past that we carry with us.
books.whyReadEn: The world that comes into view when you slow down and walk a city, block by block. A new urban novel, shaped by Sebald, that unites lyricism and intellect, stillness and restless inquiry. Perfect for readers who like their fiction to think as much as it tells.

books.title: The Novelist
books.author: Jordan Castro
books.authorJa: ジョーダン・カストロ
books.descriptionJa: ある朝、小説家は目を覚まし、スマホを開く。コーヒーを淹れ、SNSを見て、また何かを書き始める——その一日の何気ない流れを、ひたすら丁寧に追いかける実験小説。「何も起きない」が「すべてのことが起きている」文学。
books.whyReadJa: SNS時代の精神を小説で表現するとはどういうことか。フラン・オブライエンやカスクの『輪郭』の系譜を継ぐ。
books.selectionReasonJa: SNS時代の精神を小説で表現する実験文学。
books.descriptionEn: One morning, a novelist wakes up and opens his phone. He makes coffee, checks social media, feeds his cat, watches videos, and tries, in the gaps, to write. An experimental novel that traces the unremarkable, compulsive flow of a single day with obsessive, almost documentary care, refusing every dramatic gesture. It is literature in which nothing happens and, in the texture of contemporary attention, everything happens at once. A precise, funny, unsettling portrait of the mind in the age of the feed.
books.whyReadEn: What does it mean to express the inner life of the social-media age in fiction? A sharp, funny work in the lineage of Flann O'Brien and Cusk's Outline, it makes visible the constant collision between distraction and creation that defines how we live now.

books.title: Trust
books.author: Hernan Diaz
books.descriptionJa: 1920年代の金融界の帝王ベンジャミン・ラスクとその妻。彼らの富と愛の「真実」をめぐって、小説、回想録、日記、草稿という四つの異なるテクストが次々と提出される。ピューリッツァー賞受賞。真実は語り手の数だけある。
books.whyReadJa: 同じ出来事を四つの視点から見る構造の妙。読者は自分で「真実」を組み立てることになる、知的興奮の傑作。
books.selectionReasonJa: 同じ出来事を四つの視点から見る、ピューリッツァー賞受賞の知的興奮。
books.descriptionEn: Benjamin Rask, a legendary financial titan of the 1920s, and his wife Mildred, the heiress of a vast fortune—their wealth, their marriage, and the truth of their love. Around this one story, four different texts are submitted in turn: a novel, a memoir, a diary, and a draft manuscript, each contradicting and complicating the others. A Pulitzer Prize winner. The truth exists as many times over as there are narrators, and only the reader can assemble it—or decide that it cannot be assembled at all.
books.whyReadEn: The intellectual delight of a structure that views the same events from four angles, each of which distorts them differently. An intellectually thrilling masterpiece in which the reader becomes the detective, forced to weigh every account and ask who profits from each version of the truth.

books.title: The Overstory
books.author: Richard Powers
books.authorJa: リチャード・パワーズ
books.descriptionJa: 九人の人物が木との出会いをきっかけに、人生を変えられていく。彼らの物語はやがて、森を守るための抵抗運動へと収束していく。ピューリッツァー賞受賞。人間と樹木の関係を壮大なスケールで描く、環境文学の最高傑作。
books.whyReadJa: 「木と人の物語」として世界を動かした。地球環境を文学の力で考え直したい人に、必読の一冊。
books.selectionReasonJa: 木と人をめぐる、ピューリッツァー賞受賞の環境文学の最高傑作。
books.descriptionEn: Nine people, strangers to one another, each have their lives transformed by an encounter with trees: a graduate student, a programmer, a veteran, an artist, an engineer. Their separate stories gradually converge on a shared obsession and a resistance movement to defend the last great forests. A Pulitzer Prize winner. Richard Powers tells the story of the relationship between humans and trees on an epic scale, giving the non-human world a presence and a voice that few novels have ever achieved.
books.whyReadEn: A book that actually moved the world as the story of trees and people, changing how readers see the forests around them. For anyone who wants to rethink the fate of the planet through the power of literature rather than statistics, this is essential reading.

books.title: Demon Copperhead
books.titleJa: デーモン・コッパーヘッド
books.author: Barbara Kingsolver
books.authorJa: バーバラ・キングソルヴァー
books.descriptionJa: アパラチアの貧しい家庭に生まれたデーモンは、ディケンズの『デイヴィッド・コパフィールド』の現代版として、オピオイド危機のアメリカを生き抜く。ブッカー賞受賞。制度の暴力と、それでも輝く少年の生命力。
books.whyReadJa: 「アメリカの地方」と「格差」を物語として読める最重要作。500ページを一気に読ませる力。
books.selectionReasonJa: オピオイド危機のアメリカを描く、ブッカー賞受賞作。
books.descriptionEn: Demon Copperhead is born into poverty in the mountains of Appalachia, the son of a teenage mother and an absent father, and his life reads as a modern retelling of David Copperfield: orphaned, fostered, exploited, and endlessly resilient. He comes of age in the America of the opioid crisis, where the pills that promise relief destroy his community. A Booker Prize winner. It is both a furious indictment of institutional violence and a luminous portrait of a boy who refuses to be extinguished.
books.whyReadEn: The most important recent work that lets you read rural America and inequality as a story rather than a statistic. A book that pulls you through five hundred pages in one breath, it balances anger and tenderness with astonishing control.

books.title: The Book of Form and Emptiness
books.author: Ruth Ozeki
books.descriptionJa: 父を失った少年ベニーは、本が「話す」のを聞き始める。図書館で出会う奇妙な人々と、物が声を発する不思議な世界。日系カナダ人の作家オゼキが、喪失と現実逃避を禅の思想で包み込んだ、全米図書賞受賞の傑作。
books.whyReadJa: 「本がしゃべる」という設定の幻想的な小説。禅と文学の融合が心地よい。日本文化を背景にした英語文学。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「本がしゃべる」世界を描く、全米図書賞受賞作。
books.titleEn: The Book of Form and Emptiness
books.descriptionEn: After his father dies, thirteen-year-old Benny begins to hear objects speaking—and especially the books in the library, which talk to him and offer him strange, contradictory advice. He finds refuge among the odd people and things that surround him, including a young woman artist and a homeless philosopher. A National Book Award winner by the Japanese Canadian writer Ruth Ozeki, this is a novel that enfolds grief, mental illness, and the temptation of escape into the consolations of Zen thought, and it asks what it means to live with loss.
books.whyReadEn: A fantastical, gently philosophical novel built on the premise that books talk. The fusion of Zen practice and storytelling is soothing and quietly profound. It is also English literature with Japanese culture at its center, a rare and valuable combination.

books.title: Pachinko
books.author: Min Jin Lee
books.descriptionJa: 1910年代の韓国から、日本統治、戦争、そして高度成長期の日本へ。朝鮮人の一家が大阪のパチンコ産業で生き抜く四世代の物語。在日コリアンの歴史を、家族の視点から描いた大河小説。全米図書賞候補。
books.whyReadJa: 日本に生きる在日コリアンの四世代を、これほど丁寧に描いた小説は他にない。日本文学と韓国文学の間にある空白を埋める。
books.selectionReasonJa: 在日コリアン四世代を描く、日本文学と韓国文学の間の空白を埋める大河。
books.descriptionEn: Beginning in a small Korean fishing village in the 1910s, this family saga follows four generations of a Korean family through Japanese colonial rule, the war, and the years of Japan's high-speed growth. Sunja, a young woman whose life is altered by one fateful choice, becomes the ancestor of a family that must survive in the margins of Japanese society, making its living in the pachinko parlors of Osaka. A National Book Award finalist, it tells the history of zainichi Koreans from a family's point of view.
books.whyReadEn: No other novel depicts four generations of zainichi Koreans living in Japan with such intimacy and care. It fills a painful blank space between Japanese and Korean literature, and it will change how any reader sees the shared, difficult history between the two countries.

books.title: The Beekeeper of Aleppo
books.author: Christy Lefteri
books.authorJa: クリスティ・レフテリ
books.descriptionJa: シリア内戦で家も息子も失った養蜂家のノウリと妻アフラ。彼らは安全を求めて難民として海を渡り、イギリスを目指す。蜂の巣のように壊れてしまった世界で、夫婦は何を守ろうとするのか——難民の実態を描く、世界中で読まれた物語。
books.whyReadJa: ニュースでしか知らない難民問題を、個人の顔を持つ物語として体験できる。日本人読者にこそ刺さる。
books.selectionReasonJa: シリア難民の実態を個人の物語で描く、世界中で読まれた感動作。
books.descriptionEn: Nuri, a beekeeper, and his wife Afra lose their home and their son in the Syrian civil war, and Afra, blinded by grief, has stopped speaking. Together they join the tide of refugees, crossing the sea and moving through camps and borders in search of safety in Britain. In a world broken as thoroughly as a destroyed hive, the novel asks what the couple are trying to protect, and how love survives catastrophe. A story of the refugee experience read around the world, based on the author's work with refugees in Athens.
books.whyReadEn: It lets you experience the refugee crisis—known to most of us only through news headlines—as a story with individual faces, names, and inner lives. It will strike Japanese readers especially hard, and it is the kind of book that builds empathy better than any statistic.

books.title: The Last Migration
books.author: Charlotte McConaghy
books.authorJa: シャーロット・マコナギー
books.descriptionJa: 鳥たちが姿を消し、生態系が崩壊しつつある近未来。鳥類学者のフラニは、絶滅の瀬戸際にある渡り鳥たちを追って、過酷な海の旅に出る。人間の喪失と、世界の終わりをめぐる静かな寓話。環境文学の新しい名作。
books.whyReadJa: 「種の絶滅」を個人の喪失として感じられる。環境テーマを文学として読める、近年の秀作。
books.selectionReasonJa: 渡り鳥と種の絶滅を描く、環境文学の新しい名作。
books.descriptionEn: In a near future, the world's birds are vanishing and ecosystems are collapsing under the weight of human activity. Franny Stone, an ornithologist carrying a terrible private grief, is determined to follow the last migrating flock of Arctic terns on their final journey across the southern ocean—a journey that will cover tens of thousands of kilometers and cross the line between science and obsession. A quiet, luminous fable about extinction, guilt, and the end of the world, and one of the new classics of environmental literature.
books.whyReadEn: You feel the extinction of a species as a personal, intimate loss rather than an abstract crisis. A recent standout that lets you read environmental themes as literature, it is also a genuinely moving novel about grief and the human need to witness what is being lost.

books.title: A Town Called Solace
books.author: Mary Lawson
books.descriptionJa: カナダの小さな町ソレース。家出を続ける少女クララ、姉を待ち続ける大人の女性、そして事情を抱えて町に流れ着いた男。三人の孤独が静かに交差する、ブッカー賞候補の感動作。
books.whyReadJa: 「静かな小説」の力。大きな事件は起きないが、三人の心の動きが丁寧に描かれ、読後が温かい。
books.selectionReasonJa: 三人の孤独が静かに交差する、ブッカー賞候補の感動作。
books.descriptionEn: In the small Canadian town of Solace, three people are waiting, in their own ways, for something: Clara, an eight-year-old girl who keeps running away from home in a desperate bid to be noticed; Elizabeth, a grown woman who never stops waiting for her runaway sister to return; and Liam, a man who has just bought a house in town, carrying a tragedy of his own. Their three solitudes quietly converge in this Booker Prize finalist, a novel of understated tenderness and deep human warmth.
books.whyReadEn: The power of the quiet novel. Nothing dramatic happens, yet the inner movements of three hearts are drawn with such care and precision that the afterglow is genuinely warm. A gentle, moving book that restores your faith in people.

books.title: The Promise
books.author: Damon Galgut
books.authorJa: デイモン・ガルグート
books.descriptionJa: 南アフリカの白人家族スワート家。死にゆく母が黒人の使用人に「家を与える」と約束したが、その約束は守られない。四つの葬式を通して、民主化以降の南アフリカの「果たされない約束」を描く。ブッカー賞受賞。
books.whyReadJa: 「約束を守らない社会」というアパルトヘイト後の南アフリカを、家族の物語として読む。痛烈で、しかし文学的に美しい。
books.selectionReasonJa: アパルトヘイト後の南アフリカを描く、ブッカー賞受賞作。
books.descriptionEn: The Swarts are a white South African family, and the novel unfolds across four funerals over more than three decades. On her deathbed, the mother promises Salome, the Black woman who has served the household for years, that the house will be given to her—but the promise is never kept, and the family keeps failing to honor it. Through the funerals of two parents and two children, Galgut traces the unkept promises of post-apartheid South Africa itself. A Booker Prize winner with a startling, shifting narrative voice.
books.whyReadEn: Read post-apartheid South Africa—a society that made promises it has not kept—through the story of one family's moral failure. Bitter, sharp, and formally daring, yet beautiful as literature in every sentence.

books.title: The Warehouse
books.author: Rob Hart
books.descriptionJa: 世界を支配した巨大通販企業クラウド。その「倉庫」に潜り込んだ潜入調査員と、そこで働く人々。Amazon的な企業の内部を描く、現代のディストピア小説。デジタル資本主義の暗部を、サスペンスとして読める。
books.whyReadJa: 「毎日使う通販アプリの裏側」を想像できる、現代の寓話。アマゾンの倉庫労働の実態を扱った異色のエンタメ。
books.selectionReasonJa: Amazon的な企業の内部を描く、現代のディストピア小説。
books.descriptionEn: Cloud, the colossal online retailer, has come to dominate the world economy, delivering anything to anyone and housing half the country's workers in its vast fulfillment centers. Paxton, a security expert hired by the company, is sent undercover into a warehouse to find a saboteur, and inside the humming, punishing machinery of the facility he begins to see the true cost of convenience. A contemporary dystopian thriller about the dark side of digital capitalism, built on deep research into the real world of warehouse labor.
books.whyReadEn: A modern fable that lets you imagine what actually lies behind the shopping app you use every day. An unusual and gripping entertainment that takes the real conditions of Amazon warehouse work and turns them into a suspense story with genuine social bite.

books.title: Girl in Translation
books.author: Jean Kwok
books.descriptionJa: 香港からニューヨークへ移住した11歳のキンバリー。学校では秀才、放課後はチャイナタウンの工場で縫製工として働く——その二重生活。貧困と教育、移民の野望を描く、自伝的要素のある青春小説。
books.whyReadJa: 「移民の子の二重の人生」を描く力作。格差社会アメリカを下から見る、涙なしには読めない一冊。
books.selectionReasonJa: 移民の子の二重の人生を描く、格差社会の力作。
books.descriptionEn: Eleven-year-old Kimberly moves from Hong Kong to New York with her mother, who works brutally long hours in a Chinatown garment factory. Kimberly, gifted and determined, leads a double life: a brilliant student at school, and, after the bell, a seamstress working alongside her mother in the factory, living in a dilapidated apartment without heat. A semiautobiographical coming-of-age novel about poverty, education, and immigrant ambition, it follows her struggle to rise out of the trap she was born into.
books.whyReadEn: A powerful, moving portrait of the double life of an immigrant child, told from inside the experience. It shows America's unequal society from below, and it is the kind of book you cannot read without tears—or without rooting for its heroine.

books.title: Human Acts
books.author: Han Kang
books.descriptionJa: 1980年、光州民主化運動。政府軍に虐殺された人々と、遺された者たち。ハン・ガンは「人間の行為」の暴力を、複数の視点から静かに、しかし強烈に描く。ノーベル文学賞作家の、歴史と向き合う代表作。
books.whyReadJa: 『菜食主義者』で身体を描いたハン・ガンが、今度は歴史の暴力と記憶を描く。韓国現代史を知るための文学。
books.selectionReasonJa: 光州事件の記憶を描く、ノーベル賞作家ハン・ガンの代表作。
books.descriptionEn: The 1980 Gwangju uprising, and its aftermath: the students and citizens massacred by government forces, and the people left behind to live with what they saw and did. Through a chorus of voices—a boy searching for his friend's body, a woman who was forced to identify corpses, a survivor haunted by guilt—Han Kang renders the violence of human acts quietly, yet with unbearable intensity. The Nobel laureate's representative work, a novel that forces both Korea and its readers to confront history.
books.whyReadEn: Having rendered the body so unforgettably in The Vegetarian, Han Kang here turns to the violence and memory of history. Essential literature for understanding modern Korea and the price its people paid, it is also a profound meditation on what ordinary people become capable of.

books.title: Greek Lessons
books.author: Han Kang
books.descriptionJa: 声を失った女性と、目が見えていく男性。ギリシャ語の教室で出会った二人の、沈黙と対話の物語。言葉の境界と、言葉を超えた繋がりを描く、ハン・ガンの詩的な傑作。
books.whyReadJa: 「言葉を失うこと」と「言葉で繋がること」を描く、静かで深い小説。
books.selectionReasonJa: 言葉を失うことと、言葉で繋がることを描く、ハン・ガンの静かな傑作。
books.descriptionEn: A woman who has lost the ability to speak, a man who is gradually losing his sight. They meet in a Greek-language class in Seoul, and an extraordinary, silent communion grows between them—she who cannot say words and he who cannot see them. A story of silence and dialogue, of language at its limits and the connections that exist beyond words. A poetic, quietly devastating masterpiece by Han Kang, published in English to great acclaim in the year she won the Nobel Prize.
books.whyReadEn: A quiet, deep novel about losing words and about connecting through and beyond words. It is Han Kang at her most austere and most beautiful—a book to be read slowly, in silence, and to be felt long after the final page.

books.title: The White Book
books.author: Han Kang
books.descriptionJa: 死んだ姉への追悼として書かれた、白いものたちの断章。白い雪、白い米、白い光——白のイメージを通して、喪失と生をめぐる詩的な瞑想が紡がれる。ハン・ガン文学の本質に触れる一冊。
books.whyReadJa: 小説とも詩ともつかない、純度の高い文学体験。ハン・ガンの美意識の頂点。
books.selectionReasonJa: 白のイメージで喪失と生を描く、ハン・ガン文学の美意識の頂点。
books.descriptionEn: Written as a requiem for a sister who died in infancy, this is a book made of fragments, each devoted to a white thing: white snow, white rice, white bandages, white light, white swaddling cloths. Through these images of whiteness, a poetic meditation on loss, grief, and the persistence of life is slowly spun. Part novel, part memoir, part prose poem, it touches the very essence of Han Kang's literature and is among the most purely beautiful books of the twenty-first century.
books.whyReadEn: A literary experience of rare purity—neither quite novel nor quite poem, it moves in its own luminous register. The summit of Han Kang's aesthetic, it is a book you hold in your hands like a relic and finish feeling strangely, quietly healed.

books.title: We Should All Be Feminists
books.titleJa: みんなでフェミニストになろう
books.author: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
books.authorJa: チママンダ・ンゴズィ・アディーチェ
books.descriptionJa: ベイ・ヨンドルフ氏がなぜ「女性の支持者」という呼称に固執するのか。アディーチェによる、明快で力強いフェミニズム宣言。TED講演が世界中で共有され、『アメリカーナ』の読者にも読まれた。
books.whyReadJa: フェミニズム入門の最良の一冊。難解な理論書ではなく、日常から語られる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 明快で力強いフェミニズム宣言。アディーチェのTED講演が書籍化。
books.descriptionEn: Why is it that a man who champions the cause of women is described as a champion of women, while a woman who does the same is called something else entirely? In this lucid, forceful manifesto, adapted from her celebrated TED talk, Adichie draws on her own life in Nigeria and America to dismantle the everyday assumptions that keep inequality alive. Read by millions around the world, including the many readers who came to it through Americanah, it has become one of the defining feminist texts of our age.
books.whyReadEn: The best possible introduction to feminism. Not an abstruse theoretical book but one spoken from everyday life, in language anyone can enter. Short, clear, and quietly radical, it will change how you hear the word feminist.

books.title: The Committed
books.author: Viet Thanh Nguyen
books.authorJa: ヴィエト・タン・ウェン
books.descriptionJa: 『シンパサイザー』の続編。1980年代のパリに移り住んだ主人公は、両義的なアイデンティティとともに「革命的救済」の闘争に身を投じる。鋭い社会批評とユーモアが冴える。
books.whyReadJa: 『シンパサイザー』の読者が必ず読みたい続編。パリの移民社会を描く。
books.selectionReasonJa: 『シンパサイザー』の続編。パリの移民社会を描く。
books.descriptionEn: The sequel to The Sympathizer. In the 1980s, the unnamed protagonist—now a refugee in Paris—moves through a world of intellectuals, gangsters, and fellow Vietnamese exiles, trying to make a life while carrying the twin allegiances that nearly destroyed him. He becomes involved in a bookstore, a drug ring, and a violent scheme of revenge, all while the contradictions of his identity refuse to resolve. Sharp social critique, savage humor, and constant philosophical play are on full display in this sequel.
books.whyReadEn: The sequel that readers of The Sympathizer will surely want, and it delivers everything the first book promised and more. It paints Paris's immigrant society with the same corrosive intelligence, and it completes the arc of one of contemporary fiction's most fascinating narrators.

books.title: The Last Samurai
books.author: Helen DeWitt
books.descriptionJa: 天才的な母シビラと、母に語学と空手を仕込まれた息子リド。父を探して世界を旅するリドの物語。言語、知性、天才と育児をめぐる、21世紀文学のカルト・クラシック。
books.whyReadJa: 「知的で自由な小説」の代表格。村上春樹ファンにも、実験的な文学が好きな人にも。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「知的で自由な小説」の代表格。言語と知性をめぐるカルト・クラシック。
books.descriptionEn: Sibylla, a genius who was once a child prodigy, raises her son Ludo alone, teaching him six languages and martial arts and screening a single film—Seven Samurai—over and over. Fatherless, Ludo at the age of eleven sets out to find his father, testing every man he meets by asking him to finish the film's final line. A brilliant, playful novel about language, intelligence, genius, and the strange project of raising a child, and a cult classic of twenty-first-century literature.
books.whyReadEn: The very type of the intellectually free novel—joyous, erudite, and structurally daring. It rewards both Murakami fans and lovers of experimental literature, and it is one of the most purely enjoyable cult novels of the century.

books.title: The Riddle of the Labyrinth
books.author: Margalit Fox
books.authorJa: マーガリット・フォックス
books.descriptionJa: 線文字B解読の物語。考古学者エヴァンズと、解読の鍵を握った「無名の」言語学者アリス・コーバー。知性と情熱のドラマを、精緻なノンフィクションとして描く。
books.whyReadJa: 「解読」という知的冒険。コーバーの物語は、科学史に埋もれた女性の功績を蘇らせる。
books.selectionReasonJa: 線文字B解読の知的冒険。埋もれた女性科学者の功績を蘇らせる。
books.descriptionEn: In 1900, the archaeologist Arthur Evans discovered clay tablets inscribed with an undeciphered script on Crete and named it Linear B. For fifty years, the world's greatest minds failed to crack it. It was an unknown American linguist named Alice Kober who, working quietly in a Brooklyn classroom, made the crucial breakthroughs—while a brilliant rival would go on to claim the glory. A drama of intellect, obsession, and scientific detection, rendered as meticulous and gripping nonfiction.
books.whyReadEn: An intellectual adventure of the highest order: the story of a decipherment that took fifty years and almost died with its unsung heroine. Kober's story, long buried, is resurrected here with justice, and it is a powerful reminder of how many achievements have been lost to the history of science because they belonged to women.

books.title: The Botanist's Daughter
books.author: Kayte Nunn
books.descriptionJa: 19世紀の英国の植物学者の娘と、現代の古美術商。二つの時代が交差する、植物と秘密の物語。歴史ミステリと恋愛を融合した、読ませる作品。
books.whyReadJa: 植物をめぐる秘密と、二つの時代の女性たちの物語。
books.selectionReasonJa: 植物と秘密をめぐる、二つの時代の女性の物語。
books.descriptionEn: Two women, two centuries, one secret. In nineteenth-century Britain, Elizabeth, the daughter of a botanist, accompanies her father on an expedition to collect rare plants—and discovers that some secrets buried in a remote corner of the world are better left undisturbed. In the present day, Anna, an antiques dealer, inherits a mysterious notebook and follows its trail to Australia. A story of plants, passion, and buried family secrets in which the two eras slowly converge into one.
books.whyReadEn: A beautifully atmospheric blend of historical mystery and romance. Secrets surrounding plants, the lives of women across two centuries, and a puzzle that connects them—a genuinely page-turning read for fans of dual-timeline historical fiction.

books.title: The Dictionary of Lost Words
books.author: Pip Williams
books.authorJa: ピップ・ウィリアムズ
books.descriptionJa: OED（オックスフォード英語辞典）編纂の現場で、父の仕事を見て育った少女エズメ。正式な辞典から漏れた「失われた言葉」を、彼女は自分で集めていく。女性と労働者の言葉をめぐる、心温まる物語。
books.whyReadJa: 「辞書に載らない言葉」への愛。言語と権力をめぐる、ユニークな歴史小説。
books.selectionReasonJa: 辞書に載らない言葉を集める女たちを描く、言語をめぐる歴史小説。
books.descriptionEn: Esme grows up in Oxford at the turn of the twentieth century, watching her father and his colleagues compile the great Oxford English Dictionary in the Scriptorium—a world where words are collected, defined, and, crucially, decided upon. When she discovers that certain words used by women and working people never make it into the dictionary, she begins to gather them herself, in secret. A heartwarming, quietly subversive story about whose words count, and who decides what a word is worth.
books.whyReadEn: A love letter to the words that never got into the dictionary—the words of women, servants, and the poor, edited out of the record of the English language. A unique and moving historical novel about language, class, and power.

books.title: The Island of Sea Women
books.author: Lisa See
books.descriptionJa: 韓国チェジュ島の海女（ヘニョ）たちの友情と、日本統治・戦争・そして済州島四・三事件の悲劇。半世紀にわたる二人の女性の物語。女性の絆と、歴史の暴力を描く大河。
books.whyReadJa: 済州島の海女という特異な女性文化と、韓国現代史を描く傑作。
books.selectionReasonJa: 済州島の海女たちと韓国現代史を描く大河。
books.descriptionEn: On the Korean island of Jeju, the haenyeo—the women divers who support their families by harvesting the sea—are a world unto themselves. Mi-ja and Young-sook, friends since childhood, grow up to become haenyeo together, their bond forged in the freezing water and deepened by shared hardship. But the twentieth century arrives on Jeju with Japanese colonial rule, war, and the terrible events of the 1948 Jeju uprising, which will test their friendship beyond what either can bear. A sweeping, deeply researched epic of women's bonds and the violence of history.
books.whyReadEn: A masterpiece about the singular culture of Jeju's women divers and modern Korean history, from Japanese rule through the uprising that nearly destroyed the island. It is also a profound story about friendship—its durability, and its breaking point.

books.title: The Frozen River
books.author: Ariel Lawhon
books.descriptionJa: 1789年、メイン州。検死官であり助産師でもあるマーサ・バラードは、凍った川で見つかった男の死を調査し、町の秘密に迫る。実際の女性検死官を描いた、歴史サスペンスの傑作。
books.whyReadJa: 「女性の知恵」と「制度の偏見」を描く、実在人物に基づく歴史ミステリ。
books.selectionReasonJa: 実在の女性検死官を描く、歴史サスペンスの傑作。
books.descriptionEn: Maine, 1789. When the body of a man is found frozen in the river, Martha Ballard—midwife, healer, and the only woman in the town who keeps the official record of deaths—is called to examine it. As she begins to untangle the circumstances of his death, she finds herself at odds with the powerful men of the town, who would rather the truth stay buried. Based on the real diary of a real eighteenth-century woman coroner, this is historical suspense of the highest quality.
books.whyReadEn: A historical mystery built on a real person, and a superb portrait of a woman's knowledge—midwifery, medicine, and patient observation—set against the prejudice of institutions. Martha Ballard is a detective before the detective novel existed, and her story deserves to be widely known.

books.title: The River
books.author: Rumer Godden
books.descriptionJa: インドのベンガル地方で暮らすイギリス人少女ハリエット。川と共に生きる日々の中で、彼女は生と死、成長の痛みに出会う。映画化もされた、思春期の美しい古典。
books.whyReadJa: 「川」という比喩が生と死を包み込む、静かで詩的な名作。
books.selectionReasonJa: 川という比喩が生と死を包む、思春期の詩的な名作。
books.descriptionEn: Harriet, a thirteen-year-old English girl, grows up on a jute plantation in Bengal, India, beside a great river that seems to hold all the beauty and mystery of the world. The summer brings a cousin, a picnic, and a death, and through these events Harriet begins to understand the forces that will shape her life: love, grief, and the passage into womanhood. A quiet, luminous classic of adolescence, written with sensuous precision and later adapted into a celebrated film by Jean Renoir.
books.whyReadEn: A quiet, poetic masterpiece in which the river works as a metaphor that enfolds life and death, innocence and awakening. Short, precise, and deeply felt, it is one of the finest novels ever written about the border country between childhood and adulthood.

books.title: A Gentleman in Moscow
books.author: Amor Towles
books.descriptionJa: 革命後のモスクワ。軟禁された伯爵アレクサンドル・イリイチは、高級ホテル「メトロポール」から一歩も出ず、三十年を過ごす。制限された世界の中で、自由と人間性を描く、心温まる物語。
books.whyReadJa: 「狭い世界」から見える広い世界。優雅で、知性とユーモアに満ちた傑作。
books.selectionReasonJa: 軟禁された伯爵が三十年を過ごす、自由と人間性の傑作。
books.descriptionEn: Moscow, 1922. Count Alexander Ilyich Rostov, a former aristocrat, is sentenced to house arrest for the crime of being born into the wrong class—but instead of a prison cell, he is confined to the grand Hotel Metropol, where he must remain for the rest of his life. Thirty years pass inside those walls. As the world outside transforms beyond recognition, the Count finds friendship, purpose, love, and even freedom within his small domain. A warm, elegant, deeply humane story about how a life can be lived richly in the narrowest of spaces.
books.whyReadEn: A wide world seen from a narrow one. An elegant, witty, and deeply human masterpiece in which confinement becomes the occasion for grace. One of the most purely enjoyable novels of recent years, with a hero you will miss when the book ends.

books.title: The Lincoln Highway
books.titleJa: リンカーン・ハイウェイ
books.author: Amor Towles
books.descriptionJa: 1954年、ネブラスカ。少年院を出た兄弟は、故郷の農場へ戻るはずが、ニューヨークへ向かう旅に巻き込まれる。アメリカ横断の道中で出会う人々との物語。ブッカー賞候補。
books.whyReadJa: 「旅」と「物語」の力を信じる、クラシカルで温かいアメリカ小説。
books.selectionReasonJa: アメリカ横断の旅を描く、クラシカルで温かい小説。
books.descriptionEn: Nebraska, 1954. Eighteen-year-old Emmett Watson, just released from a juvenile detention farm, plans to take his young brother Billy and head west to start a new life on the family farm. But two friends from the detention farm have other ideas, and the four boys end up bound for New York City instead, driving along the Lincoln Highway in a stolen car. Over ten days of adventure, the novel weaves together their separate stories and the extraordinary people they meet. A Booker Prize finalist, it is a celebration of the journey novel and of storytelling itself.
books.whyReadEn: A classical, warm American novel that believes unapologetically in the power of journey and story. The ensemble of characters is unforgettable, and the book wears its heart on its sleeve without ever becoming sentimental. A pure pleasure to read.

books.title: The Time of the Hero
books.author: Mario Vargas Llosa
books.authorJa: マリオ・バルガス・リョサ
books.descriptionJa: ペルーの士官学校。暴力と腐敗が支配する世界で、少年たちの友情と反逆が描かれる。実際に自伝的要素を含む、ノーベル文学賞作家リョサのデビュー作にして代表作。
books.whyReadJa: ラテンアメリカ文学の巨匠の出発点。権力と暴力の構造を描く。
books.selectionReasonJa: ノーベル賞作家リョサのデビュー作。権力と暴力の構造。
books.descriptionEn: At the Leoncio Prado military academy in Lima, Peru, the cadets live in a brutal world of hazing, corruption, and violence, where the strong prey on the weak and the institution protects its own. A group of boys—including Jaguar, a secretive fighter, and Alberto, a would-be writer—are bound together by loyalty and rebellion, until a stolen exam and a betrayal set off a chain of events that leads to death. Llosa's debut novel, based on his own years at the academy and written with fierce documentary power, is also his most personal work.
books.whyReadEn: The starting point of a master of Latin American literature, and still one of his most powerful books. It lays bare the structures of power and violence with which so much of his later work would wrestle, and it reads today as a searing indictment of institutions that brutalize the young.

books.title: La fiesta del Chivo
books.author: Mario Vargas Llosa
books.authorJa: マリオ・バルガス・リョサ
books.descriptionJa: ドミニカ共和国の独裁者トルヒーヨ暗殺の三日間を、被害者・加害者・傍観者の視点から描く。独裁と抵抗、性と権力。ラテンアメリカ政治文学の最高傑作の一つ。
books.whyReadJa: 独裁者と社会の関係を、多角的な語りで描き切る。リョサ文学の到達点。
books.selectionReasonJa: 独裁者と社会を多角的に描く、リョサ文学の到達点。
books.descriptionEn: The Dominican Republic, 1961. Trujillo, the dictator who ruled the country for thirty years, is about to be assassinated. The novel unfolds across the three days of the coup, moving between the perspective of the dictator himself, the conspirators who will kill him, and Urania, a woman who returns to Santo Domingo after thirty years to confront the man who abused her family. A story of tyranny and resistance, sex and power, told with all of Llosa's narrative mastery. One of the supreme achievements of Latin American political literature.
books.whyReadEn: The relationship between a dictator and the society that produces him, rendered through brilliant multi-voiced narration that shifts seamlessly between victim, perpetrator, and bystander. A masterpiece of political fiction and a summit of Llosa's career.

books.title: The War of the End of the World
books.author: Mario Vargas Llosa
books.authorJa: マリオ・バルガス・リョサ
books.descriptionJa: 19世紀末ブラジル、カヌードスの反乱。預言者と化した男と、それを鎮圧する政府軍。社会の底辺に生まれた「王国」をめぐる、圧倒的な大河小説。
books.whyReadJa: 「狂信」と「国家」の衝突を描く、リョサの最高傑作との呼び声も高い。
books.selectionReasonJa: 狂信と国家の衝突を描く、リョサの最高傑作。
books.titleEn: The War of the End of the World
books.descriptionEn: Late nineteenth-century Brazil. In the remote backlands, a wandering preacher called the Counselor gathers a community of outcasts, former slaves, and the destitute at the settlement of Canudos, and declares it an independent kingdom under God. The fledgling Brazilian republic, seeing a threat it cannot tolerate, sends its army to crush them—again and again, with mounting losses. A sweeping, harrowing epic about faith and fanaticism, the state and the poor, and the terrible price of belief.
books.whyReadEn: Widely hailed as Llosa's masterpiece, it dramatizes the collision of religious fanaticism and the modern state with overwhelming narrative power. The siege of Canudos is one of the great set pieces of twentieth-century fiction, and the novel's questions about belief and violence remain urgent.

books.title: The Captain's Daughter
books.author: Alexander Pushkin
books.authorJa: アレクサンドル・プーシキン
books.descriptionJa: ロシアの農民反乱（プガチョフの乱）を背景に、若い将校と大尉の娘の恋を描く。ロシア文学の父プーシキンの、短く美しい歴史小説。ロシア文学の古典の原典。
books.whyReadJa: ロシア文学の原点。後のドストエフスキーやトルストイの土台を築いた一冊。
books.selectionReasonJa: ロシア文学の原点。プーシキンの短く美しい歴史小説。
books.descriptionEn: Russia, 1773. The young officer Pyotr Grinyov is sent to a remote frontier fortress, where he falls in love with Masha, the daughter of the garrison captain. When Pugachev's great peasant rebellion sweeps across the countryside, the fort is taken, the captain and his wife are executed, and Pyotr is caught between his loyalty to the state and his debt to the mysterious rebel leader who has spared his life. A short, beautifully crafted historical novel by Pushkin, father of Russian literature, and the origin of a great tradition of Russian prose.
books.whyReadEn: The origin point of Russian literature as we know it, and a perfect, compact demonstration of why Pushkin is called its father. A book that laid the foundations for Dostoevsky and Tolstoy, it is also a thrilling and deeply romantic story in its own right.

books.title: Отцы и дети
books.author: Ivan Turgenev
books.authorJa: イワン・ツルゲーネフ
books.descriptionJa: 「ニヒリスト」バザーロフ。伝統的な父世代と、科学を信奉する子世代の衝突を描き、ロシアの時代の転換点を浮き彫りにした。ツルゲーネフの代表作にして、近代ロシア小説の到達点。
books.whyReadJa: 「世代間の断絶」を描いた文学の原型。1860年代ロシアの精神史を知る。
books.selectionReasonJa: 世代間の断絶を描いた近代ロシア小説の到達点。ニヒリズムの文学化。
books.descriptionEn: Russia, 1859. Arkady Kirsanov returns from university to his father's country estate, bringing with him his friend Bazarov, a young man who calls himself a nihilist and believes in nothing but science and reason. The clash between the traditional, sentimental world of the fathers and the cold, modern certainty of the sons unfolds across love affairs, quarrels, and a duel. Turgenev's masterpiece, it threw Russia's moment of historical transition into permanent relief and gave the world a character type—the nihilist—that would echo through the century.
books.whyReadEn: The prototype of the literary treatment of the generation gap, and still one of the sharpest ever written. Bazarov is one of the great characters of world fiction. A window onto the spiritual history of 1860s Russia that reads, astonishingly, as if it were written yesterday.

books.title: Записки из мёртвого дома
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.authorJa: フョードル・ドストエフスキー
books.descriptionJa: ドストエフスキー自身のシベリア流刑体験に基づく、監獄の記録。過酷な囚人生活の中で、人間の尊厳と可能性を描く。後の大作のすべてがここから始まる。
books.whyReadJa: ドストエフスキーのリアリズムの源泉。『罪と罰』『カラマーゾフの兄弟』の背景。
books.selectionReasonJa: ドストエフスキーのシベリア体験に基づく、人間の尊厳を描く記録。
books.descriptionEn: Between 1850 and 1854, Dostoevsky was imprisoned in a Siberian labor camp for his involvement in a revolutionary circle. Out of that experience he wrote this unflinching record of prison life: the brutality of the guards, the casual cruelty and unexpected kindness of the convicts, the relentless cold and hunger, and the strange human bonds that form inside the walls. It is a book about human dignity under the worst conditions imaginable, and every great novel he wrote afterward grows out of it.
books.whyReadEn: The source of Dostoevsky's realism, and the key to everything that came after it—Crime and Punishment, The Idiot, The Brothers Karamazov all begin here. The compassion with which he renders his fellow prisoners makes it one of the most humane books ever written.

books.title: Идиот
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.authorJa: フョードル・ドストエフスキー
books.descriptionJa: 「美しい魂」の持ち主ムイシュキン公爵が、欲望と打算の渦巻くペテルブルク社会に現れる。完璧な善人は、この世界で何ができるのか。ドストエフスキーの理想と現実をめぐる大作。
books.whyReadJa: 「善人」の物語として、世界文学でも異色の傑作。罪と罰とは対照的な問い。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「善人」を主役にした、ドストエフスキーの理想と現実をめぐる大作。
books.descriptionEn: Prince Myshkin, an innocent, almost saintly young man just returned from a Swiss sanatorium, appears in a St. Petersburg society seething with money, calculation, and destructive passions. Everyone who meets him is disarmed—and undone—by his honesty, including the two women between whom he cannot choose. What can a truly good man accomplish in a world that has no use for goodness? Dostoevsky's novel of ideals and reality, widely considered one of the summits of world fiction, asks the question with unbearable intensity.
books.whyReadEn: As the story of a good man, a singular and astonishing masterpiece in world literature. It poses the question of Christ-like innocence in a modern, cynical world, in a sense the reverse of the question asked in Crime and Punishment. A book that stays with you for life.

books.title: Бесы
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.authorJa: フョードル・ドストエフスキー
books.descriptionJa: 革命を企てる若者たちと、無神論と虚無主義の陥穽。ドストエフスキーが「ニヒリズムの危険」を予言的に描いた、政治的長編小説。思想と暴力の関係を問う。
books.whyReadJa: 「イデオロギーの暴走」を描く文学の最高峰。現代の過激主義を考える先見の明。
books.selectionReasonJa: イデオロギーの暴走を予言的に描いた、ドストエフスキーの政治的長編。
books.descriptionEn: In a provincial Russian town, a group of young radicals conspires to bring down the established order through violence and manipulation, under the spell of an older revolutionary who has abandoned the movement. Dostoevsky, writing in direct response to the political terrorism of his own day, foresaw with frightening accuracy where the worship of ideas—atheism, nihilism, utopianism—could lead. A novel of ideas that is also a political thriller, a satire, and a prophecy, it remains the greatest literary diagnosis of ideology run mad.
books.whyReadEn: The summit of literature about the runaway of ideology—how a pure idea, taken seriously enough, becomes a license for murder. Its portrait of the terrorist Pyotr Verkhovensky reads like a profile of modern extremism. A book with terrifying, undiminished relevance.

books.title: Война и мир
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.descriptionJa: ナポレオン戦争を背景に、ロシアの貴族社会と庶民の群像を描く超大河小説。歴史、戦争、家族、愛——人間の営みのすべてが詰まった、世界文学の金字塔。
books.whyReadJa: 文学の「大海」。長さを恐れず、人生で一度は挑みたい世界最大の小説。
books.selectionReasonJa: 文学の「大海」。ナポレオン戦争と人間の営みすべてを描く、世界最大の小説。
books.descriptionEn: Against the vast backdrop of the Napoleonic Wars, from the drawing rooms of Petersburg to the burning of Moscow, Tolstoy follows the intersecting fates of a dozen families and hundreds of characters—nobles and peasants, soldiers and tsars, the peace-loving Pierre and the reckless Andrei and the radiant Natasha. History, war, family, love, death, and the meaning of life itself: everything human is here, rendered with an ambition and a truthfulness that no novel has matched before or since. The cornerstone of world literature.
books.whyReadEn: The ocean of literature—the greatest novel ever written, as it is so often called. Do not fear its length; it is among the most gripping stories ever told. A book that every serious reader should attempt at least once in a lifetime, and once finished, forever treasure.

books.title: The Gambler
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.authorJa: フョードル・ドストエフスキー
books.descriptionJa: ルーレットに憑かれた男の狂熱と破滅。ドストエフスキー自身の賭博体験に基づき、26日間で書き上げられたという伝説の小説。人間の「依存」と「自壊」を描く。
books.whyReadJa: 短くて読みやすいドストエフスキー。狂気の心理を描く手腕が冴える。
books.selectionReasonJa: 賭博の狂熱と自壊を描く、ドストエフスキーの短編名作。
books.descriptionEn: Alexei Ivanovich, a young tutor, is in love with the daughter of a ruined Russian general and, worse, in love with the roulette table. In the gaming rooms of the fictional spa town of Roulettenburg, his fever rises and falls with the wheel: winning, losing, staking everything on the turn of a number, unable to stop. Based on Dostoevsky's own gambling addiction and famously written in twenty-six days, this is a short, furious novel about dependence, humiliation, and the seduction of self-destruction.
books.whyReadEn: A short, fast, accessible Dostoevsky, and a brilliant portrait of addiction decades before the word existed. The psychology of the gambler—the fever, the shame, the compulsion—is rendered with chilling mastery, and the book remains uncomfortably accurate today.

books.title: Белые ночи
books.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
books.authorJa: フョードル・ドストエフスキー
books.descriptionJa: 白夜のペテルブルク。孤独な夢想家が、一晩だけ出会った少女に恋をする。ドストエフスキー初期の抒情小説。切なく、純粋で、誰の心にも残る名作。
books.whyReadJa: 「一期一会の恋」を描く、最も美しい短編。ドストエフスキーの入り口にも。
books.selectionReasonJa: 一夜の恋を描く、最も美しいドストエフスキー短編。
books.descriptionEn: In Petersburg, where summer nights never darken, a lonely young dreamer wanders the streets and, by chance, meets a girl on the canal bank. For four white nights they walk and talk together; he falls in love, and she, still faithful to a lover who has promised to return, lets him. An early lyric masterpiece of Dostoevsky, it is sweet, pure, and achingly sad—a meditation on love, loneliness, and the terrible distance between dreams and reality. A story that has stayed in the hearts of readers for over a century and a half.
books.whyReadEn: The most beautiful short work ever written about a one-night, once-in-a-lifetime love, and a perfect entry point to Dostoevsky—short, luminous, and full of feeling. It contains, in miniature, all the themes he would spend a lifetime turning over.

books.title: Middlemarch
books.author: George Eliot
books.authorJa: ジョージ・エリオット
books.descriptionJa: イギリス中部の田舎町ミドルマーチを舞台に、医師、女性、牧師など多様な市民の人生を描く。「英語で書かれた最高の小説」と称されるビクトリア朝文学の頂点。
books.whyReadJa: 「小説の完成形」と呼ばれる傑作。人間と社会の描き方の究極。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「英語で書かれた最高の小説」。ビクトリア朝文学の完成形。
books.descriptionEn: In the provincial English town of Middlemarch, the lives of a large cast of characters intersect in the years around 1832: Dorothea Brooke, an idealistic young woman who marries a dried-up scholar; the ambitious doctor Tertius Lydgate; the hypocritical banker Bulstrode; and the charming but feckless Fred Vincy. George Eliot's great novel is a vast, patient, endlessly sympathetic study of how people marry, strive, fail, and endure. Often called the greatest novel in the English language, it remains the ultimate achievement of Victorian literature.
books.whyReadEn: A masterpiece repeatedly called the perfection of the novel—the fullest, fairest, most intelligent portrait of human and social life ever committed to English prose. If you read one Victorian novel in your life, this is the one. Its wisdom about people is simply without equal.

books.title: Das Glasperlenspiel
books.author: Hermann Hesse
books.descriptionJa: 未来の「教養の国カスタリア」。全ての学問と芸術を統合する「ガラス玉演戯」の達人が、精神の楽園から現実の世界へ降り立つ。ノーベル文学賞受賞、ヘッセ晩年の最高傑作。
books.whyReadJa: 知の世界と現実の狭間を生きる。ヘッセ思想の到達点。
books.selectionReasonJa: 知の世界と現実の狭間を描く、ヘッセ晩年の最高傑作。ノーベル賞。
books.descriptionEn: In a distant future, the intellectual elite has withdrawn into Castalia, a province devoted entirely to the life of the mind, where the Glass Bead Game—a synthesis of all music, mathematics, and philosophy—is the highest art. Joseph Knecht, a genius of the Game, rises to the office of Magister Ludi at the very summit of this spiritual paradise. Then, at the height of his power, he asks whether a life of pure thought is enough, and prepares to leave the province for the world. Hesse's last great novel, for which he won the Nobel Prize, is a meditation on the life of the intellect and its limits.
books.whyReadEn: A book about living between the world of knowledge and the demands of reality, written by a master at the end of his life. The summit of Hesse's thought, it asks whether the contemplative life can justify itself, and whether wisdom is of any use outside the game. Profound, serene, and inexhaustible.

books.title: Siddhartha
books.author: Hermann Hesse
books.descriptionJa: 釈迦と同名の青年シッダールタが、悟りを求めて旅に出る。禁欲、富、愛を経て、彼が見つけるものとは。東洋思想と西洋文学が出会った、ヘッセの代表作。
books.whyReadJa: 「自己を見つめる」哲学的な物語。日本の読者にも最も読まれたヘッセ作品。
books.selectionReasonJa: 悟りを求める物語。東洋思想と西洋文学の出会い、ヘッセの代表作。
books.descriptionEn: Siddhartha, a young Brahmin in ancient India, shares his name with the Buddha—but when the Buddha passes through his town, Siddhartha chooses not to follow him. He must find enlightenment himself, through his own path: as a wandering ascetic, as a rich merchant, as a lover, as a gambler, as a ferryman beside a river. Written in luminous, simple prose, this is Hesse's meditation on the unity of all experience, East and West, and on the discovery that wisdom cannot be taught—only lived. His most beloved work in Japan and around the world.
books.whyReadEn: A philosophical story about gazing into oneself, told with Hesse's characteristic clarity and serenity. It is the Hesse work most read by Japanese readers, and no wonder: its spirit sits at the meeting point of Eastern thought and Western literature, and it offers genuine guidance to anyone searching for a self.

books.title: Demian
books.author: Hermann Hesse
books.descriptionJa: 少年エミール・シンクレアの自己発見の物語。導き手デミアンとの出会いを経て、善悪の狭間を超える「自分自身」を見つけるまで。第一次世界大戦後に書かれた、成長小説の傑作。
books.whyReadJa: 「自分とは何か」をめぐる青年の物語。ユング心理学の影響も。
books.selectionReasonJa: 自己発見を描く成長小説の傑作。ユング心理学の影響。
books.descriptionEn: Emil Sinclair, a boy from a respectable, orderly home, is drawn into the shadowy world of the town delinquent Franz Krome, and his comfortable certainties begin to crack. Then he meets Max Demian, a strange, magnetic older boy who seems to see through him, and who teaches him that good and evil are not so simply divided as his parents taught. A story of self-discovery written after the First World War, deeply marked by Jungian psychology, in which the individual must break free of family and convention to find his own law. A masterpiece of the coming-of-age novel.
books.whyReadEn: A young man's story of asking who he really is, in the face of family, school, and society. Written under the influence of Jung, it is a book about the journey from innocence to self-knowledge that has guided generations of young readers. For anyone trying to find their own path rather than follow a given one.

books.title: The Call of the Wild
books.author: Jack London
books.descriptionJa: 飼い犬バックが、金鉱探しの橇犬としてカナダの荒野へ売られ、野性へと目覚めていく。文明と自然、人間と動物をめぐる、冒険小説の古典。
books.whyReadJa: 「野生」への回帰を描く、アメリカ文学の古典。動物文学の最高峰。
books.selectionReasonJa: 野生への回帰を描く、動物文学の最高峰。
books.descriptionEn: Buck, a large, pampered domestic dog living in a California estate, is stolen and sold into the brutal world of the Klondike Gold Rush, where he must pull sleds through the frozen North. Under the whip and the frost, under the instinct of the pack and the memory of wilder ancestors, the civilized dog slowly sheds his domestication and awakens to the primordial wolf within him. A classic adventure about civilization and nature, the human and the animal, and one of the most thrilling books of American literature.
books.whyReadEn: A classic of American literature about the return to the wild, and the summit of animal literature. More than an adventure story, it is a profound meditation on instinct, freedom, and what civilization asks us to give up. Short, ferocious, and unforgettable.

books.title: The Sea-Wolf
books.author: Jack London
books.descriptionJa: 客船の沈没から救出された教養人ハンフリーは、残忍で哲学的な船長「海狼」ラーセンに捕らえられ、捕鯨船で過ごす。文明の弱さと、野性的な力の対比を描く。
books.whyReadJa: 「ニーチェ的」な船長を描いた、力強く哲学的な冒険小説。
books.selectionReasonJa: 権力と哲学を描く、ロンドンの力強い冒険小説。
books.descriptionEn: Humphrey Van Weyden, a soft, bookish gentleman of letters, is rescued from a ferry disaster by the Ghost, a sealing vessel captained by Wolf Larsen—a man of immense physical strength, ruthless cruelty, and strange philosophical brilliance. Trapped aboard the ship against his will, Humphrey is forced into the brutal work of a common seaman and, under Larsen's shadow, into an education he never sought. A powerful adventure that stages a Nietzschean confrontation between civilization and primal force, and one of Jack London's most enduring novels.
books.whyReadEn: A powerful, philosophical adventure built around a genuinely Nietzschean captain—brilliant, amoral, and terrifying. The clash between the civilized man and the lawless man of force makes it one of the great thought experiments of American literature. London's most intense novel.

books.title: White Fang
books.author: Jack London
books.descriptionJa: 野生のオオカミと犬の混血「白い牙」が、残酷な人間に飼い慣らされ、最後は愛を知る。『野性の呼び声』とは逆方向の「文明化」の物語。
books.whyReadJa: 『野性の呼び声』と対になる、動物文学の双璧。
books.selectionReasonJa: 「文明化」を描く、『野性の呼び声』と対になる動物文学の双璧。
books.descriptionEn: White Fang is born in the wild, half dog and half wolf, and learns the law of the pack: eat or be eaten. Sold into the hands of brutal men, he is trained to fight other dogs and becomes a cold, vicious, unbeatable killer. But when a kindly prospector finally wins his trust, the hardened wolf-dog must learn a new law—the law of love. The reverse journey of The Call of the Wild, in which the animal is not turned wild but tamed into civilization, it is Jack London's great companion piece to his most famous novel.
books.whyReadEn: The counterpart to The Call of the Wild—the twin summit of animal literature. Where one book turns a dog wild, this one tames a wolf into a dog, and the transformation is equally thrilling. A moving story about cruelty, trust, and the possibility of redemption.

books.title: 82년생 김지영
books.author: Cho Nam-joo
books.descriptionJa: 1982年生まれの女性キム・ジヨンの一生を、淡々とした筆致でたどる。教育、就職、結婚、出産——韓国社会で女性が経験する「当たり前の不自由」を描き、世界中で社会現象となったフェミニズム小説。
